title: 557 IT jobs are leaving Trinity Health. The work is not leaving Michigan.

chapters.headline: The work is changing employers, not disappearing
points: Starting Sunday, October 25, 557 people who keep the computers running at Trinity Health begin losing their jobs
The separations run in stages through November 29, 2026 — every position at the Livonia headquarters campus
The work — IT service desk and applications support — is moving to an outside technology company Trinity has not named
chapters.takeaway: The state's own filing says more than the press releases do — about who is affected, and whether Michigan can absorb them.

chapters.headline: An announcement in June, a number in September
points: June 18, 2026: Trinity announced the move to an outside technology partner by the end of 2026 — with no job count
September 3: the WARN notice reached the state — 557 positions, all internal technology support, none clinical or patient-facing
The notice timing is contested: a 52-day gap to the first separations, against a 60-day federal notice rule — both claims are on the record
chapters.takeaway: This is the second time Trinity has run this play in 2026 — in January it cut 10.5% of its revenue cycle workforce.

chapters.headline: Seven role families
points: The position sheet lists 129 lines of job titles; the largest family is systems administration & infrastructure: 115
Service desk & support: 76 — including the filing's largest single title, IS Service Desk Support I, at 49
Applications analysis & engineering: 68; IT management & process: 67; clinical & imaging applications: 42; identity, access & security: 36; data & database: 18
chapters.takeaway: Not a cross-section of an IT department — an entire operating layer, lifted out at once.

chapters.headline: The filing's own numbers do not add up
points: The position sheet's lines sum to 422 — the seven families above are the whole published list
The total printed at the bottom of the same document — the figure in the state's notice and every headline — is 557
That leaves 135 people inside the total with no title anywhere in the published list
chapters.takeaway: We do not know why, and the document does not say — the benign possibilities are stated as possibilities only; none is endorsed.

chapters.headline: The openings exist; the timing does not work
points: Computer user support specialists: 1,530 projected openings a year statewide, growth 2.0%, wages $22–$32 an hour
Computer systems analysts: 1,045 openings a year, growth 6.8%, $38–$58 an hour; CIS managers: 1,115 openings, growth 12.4%, $58–$84
Information security analysts: only 255 openings a year — but the fastest growth on the list, 25.6%; software developers: 3,360 openings, growth 20.4%
chapters.takeaway: Openings are a flow spread across twelve months and the whole state; 557 people in one metro enter the same segment inside a five-week window.

chapters.headline: Health-IT experience itself
points: The deepest demand is adjacent to these workers: security (up 25.6%) and software development (up 20.4%)
Trinity runs on Epic, the dominant hospital platform — Corewell Health and Henry Ford Health hire Epic analysts continuously
Constraints: Wayne County unemployment stood at 6.9% in August 2026, and at least four health systems outsourced IT in 2026 — UnityPoint Health's 207 roles in April among them
chapters.takeaway: An Epic analyst at Trinity is not starting over at Corewell or Henry Ford — they are changing buildings. That helps one family much more than the others.

chapters.headline: Real machinery, slower than the schedule
points: Michigan Works! (SEMCA, for Wayne County) and the federal Dislocated Worker program: training capped at $5,000 per participant, work-based training at $10,000
Michigan Reconnect pays community-college tuition for residents 25 and older with no prior degree

Schoolcraft College, in Livonia itself, teaches the exact credentials this market asks for; the Going PRO Talent Fund reimburses employers roughly $2,000 per trainee, $3,500 for registered apprenticeships
chapters.takeaway: The pathways are real, and they are slower than the separation schedule — that gap is the actual workforce problem in this story.

chapters.headline: The vendor's name, and where the roles land
points: First, the vendor's name — the single most consequential unknown in the story
Second, whether the vendor's roles are local: a transfer of employer, or an export of 557 jobs
Third, the notice dispute — whether the 60-day requirement was met will be sorted out by people with the actual notice dates
chapters.takeaway: On November 30, a nurse in one of 91 hospitals will still call a service desk when the system fails. The open question is who answers — in Michigan, or not.
